# --include-uncovered-nodes runs the mutants the coverage pre-pass saw no
# test reach, which are skipped without it.
#
# The test below renders the page for a guest only, so nothing it runs
# reaches the {{.Secret}} inside {{if .Admin}}. With the flag that mutant
# runs, and is missed; -v still lists it under "no test reaches", so the
# miss reads as an untested branch rather than a weak assertion, and the
# summary says the unreached mutants were run. The JSON report records
# the flag.

! muxt test-template-mutations -v --seed 1 --include-uncovered-nodes
cmp stdout want.txt
! stderr 'warning:'
! stderr 'tests fail under'

! muxt test-template-mutations --seed 1 --include-uncovered-nodes --format json
stdout '"include_uncovered_nodes": ?true'
stdout '"skipped": ?0'

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.27
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "page"}}Hello, {{.Name}}!{{if .Admin}} {{.Secret}}{{end}}{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Page struct {
	Name   string
	Admin  bool
	Secret string
}

func Render(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "page", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestGuestPage(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Page{Name: "Ada", Secret: "s3cret"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "Hello, Ada!"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("page = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
